the Grok Bot team ships quality at an incredible pace! we've invested in making our code friendly for agents, by making the easy thing the right thing. 

engineers, designers, and PMs all contribute multiple hundreds of PRs a day: fixing bugs, polishing the user experience, and making our apps faster and more reliable. it isn't perfect of course and we do make mistakes, but we aim to learn from each occurrence and improve our workflows so our bots don't make the same mistake twice.

i personally think that Grok Bot is the best example today in the industry of where all those tokens are going: quality and velocity, without compromise. something i think people forget in the discussion around token usage is that software development is an iceberg - new features are only a small fraction of the work in maintaining high quality software. 

and we will keep accelerating and improving!

note_tweet.text:
For the past 6 months openclaw has been my go-to agent running huge parts of my daily life. I forced myself to give grok bot a try for the last 10 days and I've been blown away.

I really thought this would be another failed attempt to try a new bot. But grok bot got me, I'm hooked, I've moved everything over.

Here's what changed my mind:

(1) Voice calls

Being able to have a conversation with my bots is such a natural way to work with them. I'd previously loved using codex's voice mode but grok bot takes it to another level because you're talking to your agents with all of your context.

I've come to associate different voices with my different bots. And I'm at a point now where I'm running daily standups with my bots to review what's been done, unblock, and plan what's next, all via voice.

(2) Multi-threaded conversations

The way grok bot handles multiple threads in the same conversation is really impressive. You know when you're texting a friend and you've got a few topics going at once, so you're replying to one while they're replying to another? Grok bot can chat like that.

Going multi-threaded makes chat feel far more natural. It also removes the urge to create a duplicate agent just to have a second thread going.

(3) Multi-agent collaboration

The way that my different bots work with each other kinda blew my mind the first time I saw it. My main agent along with a team of specialists will often collaborate to get a job done. For example, one agent that triages my inbox will collaborate with other specialist agents to make a decision about whether to raise the email to me immediately, include it in my daily standup, or archive it.

Specialization makes problems easy to diagnose and the way agents collaborate massively reduces the amount of noise I have to process. In many ways, working with my bots feels like working with a team of humans.

(4) Harness x model

This is the one I was most anxious about. I love openclaw's openness. The ability to select my own model, thinking mode, speed, etc is what kept me with openclaw for so long.

But I have to say, whatever the grok bot team is doing just feels right. I get quick answers to simple questions and well thought through answers to more complex problems. And, when writing code, my bots will delegate to cursor, which gives the control needed for the most complex scenarios.

Kudos to the grok bot team. Now it’s time to do daily standup with my agents.

note_tweet.text:
extremely impressed by grok @bot. random musings on it and some of the competition:

- native apps far superior to the imessage (e.g. instinct) form factor. imessage is easier to bootstrap for normies and simpler onboarding, but for any reasonable power usage, a dedicated native app is just better.
- multi-bot model (e.g. grokbot) is superior to single bot model (e.g. dots). its a tad more daunting, but creating specialist bots with their own identities/rules/routines is more fun, makes me feel incentivized to invest more in each, and is generally less overwhelming than having a dumpster ground of unrelated topics in one thread. the downside of this model is that i often forget which bot i was talking to about something and revert to my main bot as a router.
- other than multibot, some key things that make Grok Bot great: multi-device (ios, mac, tesla), super performant (so fast and responsive), exhaustive ecosystem integrations and mcp support. it just works every time.
- claude duet is def on to something with the 'tasks' tab. recognizing todos, structuring them, showing status in a familiar mental model like a todolist, and allowing one-click actions feels very natural and magical. excited to play with it. don't have access yet. 
- openai shipping dots as a section within the main chatgpt app was a mistake imo. it's out of sight and fighting the existing user behavior / muscle memory of how people use chatgpt (which is already conflicted and confused between codex/chatgpt work & chatgpt). dots should have been a separate app and should subsume the o.g. chatgpt use case. what can chatgpt do that dots can't? there should just be Dots and Codex as two separate apps (this is not a statement on what they should each be named). i can imagine the OAI team faced an extremely complicated set of trade-offs when weighing this, and i empathize, but imo there's a much better end state to be had. 

caveat that i haven't in earnest tried using muse yet, and I haven't been motivated to invest in porting other than occasionally feeling inspired by @alexandr_wang's shitposting.
